items.title: Spotify DJ gets new voices, and the ability to stop yammering
items.excerpt: Spotify's AI DJ adds eight more English voices in various accents and two Spanish voices, plus an option to turn off the commentary entirely.
items.rationale: New feature release on the biggest streaming platform: ten new AI DJ voices and an option to turn the commentary off change how listeners use the AI DJ.

items.title: VSL introduce Vienna Performer
items.excerpt: Vienna Symphonic Library's Vienna Performer is an AI-powered plugin that takes a user's MIDI part and renders it with modelled phrasing, bowing, breath, vibrato and timing; models were trained only on VSL's own Synchron Stage recordings and there is no generative note output.
items.rationale: New plugin release: AI performs the composer's own MIDI with realistic phrasing instead of writing notes, and it was trained only on VSL's own recordings. Orchestral mock-up work changes from tomorrow.

items.title: NeuTone Launches NeuSynth, an AI Stem Generator That Creates New Instrument Layers from 60 Seconds of Audio in Your DAW
items.excerpt: Korean AI audio startup NeuTone announced NeuSynth, an in-DAW plugin that analyses about 60 seconds of a track and generates new instrument stem layers that fit it.
items.rationale: New in-DAW tool: it generates matching instrument stems from a minute of a track, so producers can add layers inside their sessions.

items.title: 존박·곽진언 '맥도날드 주문 랩', 해외 음원 플랫폼에 무단 등록…작사·작곡자도 제3자
items.excerpt: John Park and Kwak Jin-eon's viral 'McDonald's order rap' was uploaded to Spotify and YouTube Music by an unknown act with third-party credits, with an added rap in a John Park-like voice raising suspicion of generative-AI voice cloning.
items.rationale: A new, concrete case of a viral clip hijacked onto streaming services with a suspected AI voice clone and false credits. It shows the distribution-fraud risk artists face.

items.title: AI-music labelling 'can't be just the platforms' says RIAA boss
items.excerpt: RIAA chief Mitch Glazier told The Verge's Decoder that labelling AI music can't fall only on DSPs, outlining the industry's view on disclosure and voice rights.
items.rationale: The US label body sets out its position that AI-music disclosure must go beyond the streaming platforms. That shapes who will carry the labelling burden next.
